note: Snapshot files are reproducible extracts of free, openly licensed public data. sha256 values are of the files in this directory. Raw downloads are not all committed; their URLs and licences are recorded here. No paid API and no fabricated rows.

files.title: Australian Road Deaths Database fatalities
files.publisher: Bureau of Infrastructure and Transport Research Economics (BITRE)
files.notes: Extracted from bitre_fatalities_sep2026.xlsx sheet BITRE_Fatality (title rows removed). From May 2025 BITRE no longer publishes a separate fatal-crashes file; crash attributes are on each fatality row and fatal crashes are the distinct Crash ID values. Recent months are preliminary.

files.title: Quarterly estimated resident population by state, sex and age
files.coverage: 2017 Q4 to 2026 Q1, states and Australia, persons by single year of age plus male and female totals
files.notes: ABS Data API dataflow ERP_Q, measure 1 (estimated resident population), no API key. Five-year age aggregates were dropped so single years are not double-counted. The newest quarter in this extract is 2026 Q1 (31 March 2026).

files.title: Annual estimated resident population by SA4
files.coverage: Statistical Area Level 4, 30 June 2018 to 30 June 2025, ASGS Edition 3
files.notes: ABS Data API dataflow ABS_ANNUAL_ERP_ASGS2021, region type SA4, measure ERP. Free, no API key.

files.title: Victoria fatal and serious-injury crashes
files.publisher: Department of Transport and Planning, Victoria
files.coverage: Fatal and serious-injury crashes from 1 January 2018. Source file runs to 28 March 2026; 2026 is partial.
files.notes: Subset of the Victorian Road Crash Data flat file: fatal and serious-injury crashes only, analysis columns only. Other-injury crashes were left out to keep the snapshot small. This is a state collection and is not the same count as BITRE deaths.

files.title: Australia state and territory outlines
files.coverage: 1:50m admin-1 polygons for the eight states and territories
files.notes: The ABS ArcGIS boundary service returned an error on the access date, so the dashboard ships these public-domain outlines. Coordinates are rounded to three decimal places. Jervis Bay Territory is omitted. Statistical numbers do not come from this file.

files.title: National Road Safety Strategy target rules
files.publisher: Office of Road Safety / Department of Infrastructure
files.licence: Published Australian Government policy parameters, reproduced with attribution
files.coverage: Headline 2021–30 targets used to draw the path. Death counts are computed from BITRE, not copied.
files.notes: Parameters only: 50 percent fewer deaths and a 55 percent lower per-person rate by 2030, against the 2018–2020 average, on a straight path. The Strategy does not set state targets; state paths apply that same national rule to each state's own baseline, which is how the AAA NRSS benchmark reads jurisdictional progress.
